title: Memory-pressure-aware probe coordinator to reduce autoscaler thrash
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We observed recent regional thrashing where nodes oscillate between Ready/NotReady driven by memory growth during heavy inference workloads. The standard readiness/liveness probes marked instances unhealthy while they were still serving (large KV cache ramps, transient heap spikes), triggering the autoscaler to kill/recreate pods and causing cascading SLO violations.

Goal: Implement a probe coordinator layer that makes probe decisions memory-pressure-aware so that readiness and liveness transitions are smoothed during transient heap/RSS events, reducing autoscaler churn and preserving SLOs (p99 latency and error budget).

Scope:
- Add a lightweight memory headroom metric (RSS & jvm/alloc metrics where applicable) to probe evaluation.
- Implement progressive probe backoff windows driven by memory trend (grow/decay), not just failure count.
- Classify probes into cheap (tcp/port), functional (synthetic inference), and expensive (full-model GET) with different backoff policies.
- Expose probe-decision signals to the autoscaler so autoscale decisions can derate on memory-pressure vs hard-failure.
- Instrument dashboards and alerts for pre/post rollout validation.

Out-of-scope: Rewriting autoscaler core; large infra changes to memory limits for nodes. Those will be follow-ups informed by telemetry from this work.
acceptance_criteria: Probe coordinator reads per-pod memory headroom metric and applies backoff logic without adding >1ms median probe latency
Autoscaler receives a probe-decision rationale tag (e.g., 'memory-derated', 'hard-failed') and will not immediately kill pods when decision is 'memory-derated'
End-to-end e2e test simulating KV-cache ramp shows at least 60% reduction in pod churn compared to baseline during test window
No regression in fast-failure detection: deliberate container OOMs still clear readiness <10s after proof-of-concept rollout in staging
Dashboards show clear memory-trend-driven probe events and a post-rollout drop in SLO error budget consumption during stress tests
implementation_steps: Design probe coordinator API (read-only) that ingests probe results + memory headroom signal and emits final readiness/liveness decision
Instrument runtime to publish per-container RSS and heap-growth-rate metrics to existing agent (metrics prefix 'runtime.mem.headroom' and 'runtime.mem.growth_rate')
Implement coordinator with configurable rule engine: thresholds, ramp-duration, and classification weights for probe types
Wire coordinator output to autoscaler admission controller: add 'probe_reason' tag to health events and add 'derate' flag for autoscaler logic
Create unit tests for coordinator rules + integration tests against a simulated runtime that can mimic cache warmups and OOMs
Add dashboards/alerts and a staging canary rollout (10% nodes) behind feature flag for 48h observation
Collect telemetry and iterate on thresholds; create follow-up tasks for autoscaler tuning if necessary
risks: Overly permissive backoff could hide true failures leading to extended SLO violations — mitigate with conservative defaults and staging canary
Incorrect memory headroom estimation on some runtimes (e.g., JNI or unusual allocator behavior) — mitigate by validating headroom metric across platforms
Coordination lag between apps emitting memory metrics and coordinator reading them could produce stale decisions — mitigate by using short TTLs and fallback to existing probe evaluation
Increased complexity in autoscaler logic may require synchronization with ops and on-call teams to update runbooks
metrics_to_track: probe_transition_rate (Ready->NotReady count per pod per hour)
p95/p99 request latency and error-rate during canary windows
postmortem_links: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-02-11-pod-thrash - incident writeup that motivated this change
tests: Unit: rule engine evaluation matrix covering growth_rate x base_probe_result combinations
Integration: synthetic KV-cache ramp scenario run in k8s-like harness (10 pods, 30m) comparing pod churn with/without coordinator
Chaos: OOM injection test to ensure quick hard-fail path remains intact
rollout_plan: Enable in staging cluster, run 48h smoke + stress tests
Canary rollout 10% of nodes in us-west for 72h with elevated observability
If metrics pass (pod_churn_rate down, no increase in p99 errors), ramp to 50% then 100% over 7 days
If any regression observed, rollback via feature flag and page on-call rotation 2
